rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes adding oxide particles (Y2O3) to a generic RHEA, while the paper compared a Re-containing equiatomic film with a Re-free film. This is a different kind of intervention (composition change via Re vs. oxide dispersion).
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies high-temperature (900-1000°C) and irradiation, whereas the paper used room-temperature deposition, He-ion irradiation, and room-temperature mechanical testing. These are different regimes.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes oxide particles pinning dislocations and grain boundaries to reduce creep and delay radiation damage, while the paper's mechanism relies on grain refinement, lattice distortion, excess free volume, and amorphous grain-boundary regions acting as defect sinks to suppress He-bubble growth. These are different general classes of mechanism.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts increased yield strength and improved irradiation resistance, while the paper's outcome is reduced irradiation hardening and grain-boundary embrittlement. Both involve improved mechanical performance under irradiation, but the specific property (yield strength/ductility vs. hardening/embrittlement) and direction differ in detail.
